# Ho-Smart v0.2.8 — Quiet hours on the receiver device page

**Focus:** Replace confusing sequential Configure forms with direct Home Assistant receiver/channel switches, time pickers and scheduling selectors. Restore everyday device controls to the device page while retaining the verified Ho-Smart & eMACROS integration identity.

## Why this release exists

In v0.2.7 the nightly schedule settings lived in a two-stage Configure flow: receiver settings first, then multiple channel fields. People had to repeatedly enter configuration to adjust a night schedule, and some reported that the next channel only appeared after saving the previous one. This release removes that interface entirely. **Configure is now for connection mode, not quiet hours.** All schedules can be edited on the device itself.

## Improvements and fixes

- Each Local/Hybrid receiver shows **Receiver overnight quiet hours** (enable switch), **Receiver quiet starts**, **Receiver quiet ends**, and **Receiver quiet-hours action** as standard Home Assistant entities.
- Channels 1–4 are visible together from the start, each with an **overnight behavior selector** and **quiet starts/ends** time pickers. Select **Follow receiver-wide hours**, **Always armed (protected)**, or **Disarm on custom schedule (stops detection)**.
- Add direct **Channel 1–4 armed** switches that attempt local arm/disarm with acknowledgement and post-write state readback. Unlike status sensors, these are actionable controls.
- Schedule changes are stored in the same existing config-entry options and are applied in place without reloading/reconnecting the receiver. Changing Channel 2 does not overwrite Channel 1.
- Restart-safe restoration intent and the previous 10 PM–7 AM receiver default are retained. Protected channels continue to block global mute/power-off when they should remain audible.
- Add isolated standard-library regression tests for channel independence, settings validation, safe defaults and avoiding unnecessary options writes.

## What this release does not do

**Per-channel quieting disarms the channel; it does not merely reduce that channel's audio volume.** The HS006W exposes a shared receiver Volume control and ZoneAlarming flags, not verified per-channel audio volume. Disarming can prevent physical events and cloud reporting. Do not disable sensors essential to safety, entry notification, or an always-active driveway.

**Actual firmware write behavior remains unverified.** Property-write protocol support does not prove the HS006W will accept the vendor-specific partial JSON updates. The integration validates responses and reads values back, reports failures in logs/status, and uses bounded retries. Receiver power-off can also disconnect Wi-Fi and prevent remote restoration. Test with the device physically accessible.

No additional eMACROS model is certified by this user-interface release. Ho-Smart and eMACROS names coexist, but other receiver models require independent verification. Existing integration domain `hosmart`, entity unique IDs and stored credentials are preserved.

## Installation and upgrade

1. Update **Ho-Smart & eMACROS for Home Assistant** to v0.2.8 in HACS and restart Home Assistant.
2. Open **Settings → Devices & services → Ho-Smart & eMACROS → Devices → [your receiver]**.
3. Under **Configuration**, find the master quiet-hours switch, start/end time entities, quiet action, and **Channel 1–4** behavior/time entities. All channels appear together; there is no Configure wizard to step through.
4. For an always-on driveway channel, choose **Always armed (protected)**. For channels you intend to stop receiving alarms overnight, select **Disarm on custom schedule** (or inherit the receiver schedule), and edit the relevant times.
5. Verify the receiver's own behavior and **Night quiet status** diagnostics during supervised testing before relying on automation.

Existing schedules migrate automatically because the existing entry options are reused unchanged. Cloud-only mode cannot expose the local receiver-write controls.
